time_precision: Host clock on the immediately preceding primary-source pin, before any search in this target.
target: Decide existence of BTD(12,15;6,2,10;8,6): an unrestricted 12-by-15 matrix with entries 0,1,2, each row containing exactly six ones and two twos, every column summing to eight, and distinct rows having inner product six.

primary_attestation.open: Rosin arXiv:2501.17725v1 (29 Jan 2025), Table 1, layout lines92-119: the row (12,15;6,2,10;8,6)? is listed among the Handbook's smallest open instances, with no progress. The May2025 follow-up arXiv:2505.23881v1 Table1(a) solves seven BTDs, not this one. The current public CPro1 definition file still lists this target; scout InfoNextScreen3 found no later construction. A miss is not novelty; the Handbook table itself was not accessed.
primary_attestation.definition: Francel-Hurd, Nested balanced ternary designs and Bhaskar Rao designs, Australas. J. Combin.42 (2008)3-19, pp3-5: a BTD is a collection of B multiset blocks, incidence entries0/1/2, fixed row counts rho1,rho2, column sum K and pairwise row inner product Lambda. Simple (no repeated blocks) is explicitly an additional condition (layout lines124-125); it is NOT imposed here. Repeated columns are allowed.
primary_attestation.sources: review/btd12-15-parent-source-screen-v1/manifest.json (Rosin Jan/May PDFs and layout text, Francel-Hurd primary definition, CPro1 definition file).
primary_attestation.information_science_scope: Finite ternary code/experimental-design existence: the rows have fixed composition and Gram matrix 8I+6J. The link is combinatorial/statistical design, weaker than the preceding covering-code target; do not present it as a communication-theory breakthrough.

exact_quantifiers.matrix: All 12x15 matrices over{0,1,2}; no automorphism, cyclicity, prescribed column types, distinct-column, resolvability or block-orbit assumption.
exact_quantifiers.equivalent_invariants: Row sum10, row squared norm14, six ones and two twos; column sums8; M M^T =8I+6J. Row sum alone and Gram matrix alone do NOT replace the fixed row-composition conditions.
exact_quantifiers.symmetries: Permuting rows and columns preserves existence. Fixing one row to seven0s, six1s and two2s in that order is complete by column permutation. Any further lexicographic, partition or orbit reduction requires a written completeness argument before exclusion.

first_obligations: Read the pinned primary definition and attestation, recheck bounded later status, then freeze README attack/representation before any substantial search.

Write a strict definition-first stdlib witness verifier and an independent native checker; calibrate with explicit BTD(3,3;1,1,3;3,2), rows(2,0,1),(1,2,0),(0,1,2), plus at least one published CPro1 BTD, intended-reason row-count/column-sum/pair-product/range mutations. No import of CPro1's verifier.

Start with an unrestricted CP-SAT witness search with native wall-time limits, and/or a complete SAT/PB encoding suitable for proof checking. Record every symmetry/pruning condition. A heuristic miss, timeout, CP-SAT INFEASIBLE without independent proof, or restricted-model UNSAT does not settle nonexistence.

acceptance.existence: One strict-format full matrix passing the parent definition-first checker, two independently authored further checker routes, intended-reason controls, producer/seed replay and source comparison. Matrix format: BTD 12 15 6 2 10 8 6 on line1, followed by exactly12 lines of15 space-separated0/1/2 entries, finalLF; no unparsed data. Report duplicate columns separately, not as a rejection.
acceptance.nonexistence: A complete unrestricted encoding with a written correctness/completeness proof, and independently checked DRAT/LRAT or equivalent exact proof; a second independently written encoding or a mathematical contradiction. Native solver limits; interrupted proof checks are UNKNOWN, never an exclusion.
acceptance.claim: Settles one explicitly listed finite existence case only; no asymptotic theorem, all-BTD classification, or model-comparison claim.

bounded_plan: Initial assay <=3h with host-clock checkpoints<=30min. At most4 CPU workers,8GiB RAM,10GiB new data. Native solver/time limits or SIGTERM plus bounded wait only, no SIGKILL or subprocess.run(timeout=...). If exhausted, record a concrete obstruction and changed representation before another long run.
